title: test_scratch_cannot_outlive_its_process mints its dead minter with a subprocess, not os.fork, so its sweep teeth run on Windows
intention: The three teeth of test_scratch_cannot_outlive_its_process.py that fork a minter (test_a_seal_sweeps_first_and_says_so, test_a_killed_minter_is_swept_with_its_delivery_companion, test_the_sweep_never_touches_a_live_table) use a subprocess child and run on Windows.
why: Measured 2026-11-14 on akiendell: test_scratch_cannot_outlive_its_process.py reads 4 failed, 2 passed: three of the failures are AttributeError os.fork (lines 127 and 158) and one is test_the_moved_proofs_stay_green (the moved proofs' own bus reds). os.fork does not exist on Windows, so the proofs that simulate a dead minter with a forked child cannot run there, and the Windows sweep (store.process_start read /proc and answered None for every pid) had NO tooth until 5b940b1c4fbe's own proof: the bug stood undetected as long as the only sweep proofs were POSIX-only.
traces_to: Law 8 (a proof that cannot run on a box proves nothing there), Law 3.
how: Replace the os.fork child with subprocess.Popen of a small python child that mints the scratch table and exits or is killed, keeping every assertion the proof makes; red-first is the AttributeError today, green once the child is a subprocess and 5b940b1c4fbe's Windows branch is in.

measured.saw: test_scratch_cannot_outlive_its_process.py reads 4 failed, 2 passed: three of the failures are AttributeError os.fork (lines 127 and 158) and one is test_the_moved_proofs_stay_green (the moved proofs' own bus reds).
measured.how: census_sweep_run.py: the proof run plain on a worktree of origin/main and on win-process-start; AttributeError: module 'os' has no attribute 'fork'

outcomes.claim: the three forked-minter teeth run on Windows and read green, over a real sweep

outcomes.text: the subprocess child replaces os.fork in the proof; every assertion stays.
outcomes.claim: with os.fork taken away, as on Windows, the proof's _fork_minter (a subprocess child, name kept) still mints a scratch table the next sweep drops after a kill, and _dead_pid still names an exited pid; every assertion of the three minter teeth stays
